turns.content: For triangle ABC, we know BC = 12 and ∠B = 30°; let AC = b and AB = c. Which side is opposite the known angle, and which quantities are fixed?
Derive an equation in c using the given 30° angle, and determine when two distinct real values of c exist.
Use the root sum and product to determine when both possible values of c are positive.
Check whether either boundary value gives two distinct positive lengths.
List the admissible integer values of b.
Count the integer cubic units of AC for which two distinct positive values of AB are possible.
